geometry.derivationNote: The A2 documentary publication source-verifies the treaty and its enumerated boundary landmarks. Reconstruct the southern segment from the treaty's named rivers, bogs, stones, lakes and other landmarks. The sparse northern segment must remain a frontier/boundary corridor with uncertainty instead of a falsely exact line until the named landmarks are securely identified.

territoryChanges.notes: The legal demarcation is source-verified; exact modern placement of all medieval landmarks remains a separate geometry task.

geometry.derivationNote: The A1 archival treaty source-verifies the 12 July 1711 settlement and the return of Azov with its associated fortresses to Ottoman possession, together with related fortification obligations. Exact affected-area geometry remains pending reconstruction from the treaty, implementation records and period cartography; legal cession must not be represented by a modern administrative polygon.

territoryChanges.notes: EBID also indexes Peter I's ratification of the Pruth treaty on 12 July 1711. The legal settlement is therefore source-backed independently of the still-pending exact area geometry.

geometry.derivationNote: The A1/A2 documentary record source-verifies the 13 June 1713 Russo-Ottoman follow-up peace settlement. Its post-Pruth boundary consequences must still be reconstructed clause-by-clause against the 1711 settlement and implementation/demarcation records before any exact area or line geometry is promoted.

territoryChanges.notes: This promotion verifies the treaty-level territorial settlement only; it does not claim that the complete post-1713 southern border has been georeferenced.

geometry.derivationNote: The treaty source-verifies Japan's renunciation of rights to all Sakhalin in favor of Russia, effective for replay at the documented exchange of ratifications. This is a legal-status recognition layer; exact island coastline/area geometry must come from period cartography and must not be inferred from a modern Sakhalin polygon.

territoryChanges.notes: Moved from signature to the official 22 August 1875 ratification exchange recorded by the Japanese Foreign Ministry.

geometry.derivationNote: The treaty source-verifies cession to Japan of the enumerated Kuril islands from Shumshu through Urup. Build the area change from those named historical island units, not from a generalized modern archipelago polygon.

territoryChanges.notes: Legal cession is source-verified at ratification exchange; island-by-island period coastline geometry remains pending.

effectiveDate.note: Article 29 states that the parties regard themselves as formally bound from ratification; FRUS reports the exchange at St Petersburg on 17 March 1878.

geometry.derivationNote: The preliminary territorial clauses became legally operative at ratification, but this state is explicitly temporary and later superseded by the Berlin settlement. Exact Caucasus/Balkan geometry requires the treaty's boundary clauses and explanatory map; it must not be materialized as a permanent post-1878 border.

territoryChanges.notes: Temporary legal state only, from 17 March 1878 until superseded by the Berlin settlement.

effectiveDate.note: The Berlin ratification procès-verbal records the exchange on 3 August 1878 and the Ottoman declaration that the treaty was valid from that date.

geometry.derivationNote: Article 58 source-verifies the Ottoman cession to Russia of Ardahan, Kars and Batum with associated territories. Exact acquired-area geometry must be georeferenced from the treaty boundary clauses and contemporary demarcation maps/records.

territoryChanges.notes: Berlin supersedes the provisional San Stefano territorial state; replay is moved from signature to the documented ratification exchange.

effectiveDate.original: 15 октября 1905 г. — вступление Портсмутского договора в силу
effectiveDate.note: Signature was 23 August (5 September) 1905. Article XIV ties entry into force to the later ratification notification; U.S. Department of State International Boundary Study No. 17 records 15 October 1905 as the date the treaty came into force.

geometry.derivationNote: Article IX fixes 50° N as the legal limit of the ceded territory. The official Japanese 1940 statistical table, citing Hydrographic Department survey data, publishes the border endpoints as 142°09′25″ E and 143°59′40″ E. The line is generated as a rhumb/parallel segment retaining those historical source coordinates literally. No unsourced WGS84 datum transformation is applied.

territoryChanges.notes: This verifies the boundary line only. It does not promote the full South Sakhalin cession polygon or its coastline to geometry-verified status.
